title: Session primer injection probe
body:
Goal:
- Define a lightweight, secure mechanism to inject "primers" (short context snippets / hints) into active sessions without breaking session affinity or KV cache semantics. This is an exploratory sketch for an experiment driving improved cold-start quality for conversation flows.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Some conversation flows suffer from poor continuity when a new session attaches to a model runtime (cold KV cache). A small, authenticated primer that seeds the session with a condensed state (system instruction, recent turn-summary, user preferences) can reduce token throughput and improve early-turn quality.
- We need a minimal API + runtime contract that:
  * is safe to apply mid-session
  * is replayable for diagnostics
  * does not invalidate cached KV chunks for unrelated callers

High-level design options considered:
1) Ingress-level injection: edge proxy accepts POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/primer and attaches "primer ops" into the session queue before the next user message arrives.
   + Pros: cheap, avoids altering runtime request path.
   - Cons: must guarantee ordering and TTL; race conditions if user request inflight.
2) Session-manager mediated: session-manager exposes a primer RPC; it coordinates with runtime to apply primer as a synthetic input and update session metadata.
   + Pros: can ensure atomicity w.r.t KV cache updates.
   - Cons: more coupling and implementation scope.
3) Client-side prewarm tokens: return a short one-time "primer token" that clients present in the first generation call; runtime applies primer on token consumption.
   + Pros: simple runtime semantics.
   - Cons: requires client changes and token lifecycle.

Sketch chosen for probe (v0): hybrid ingress + best-effort session-manager handshake. Rationale: we can iterate quickly by adding a pre-step in edge proxy and later shift semantics fully into session-manager.

API shape (v0):
POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/primer
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer <session-admin-token>  // token scope = primer:write
  X-Request-Id: <uuid>
Body (application/json):
{
  "primer": "short text or compressed base64 blob",
  "scope": "user|session|tenant",
  "priority": "normal|high",
  "ttl_seconds": 60,
  "apply_mode": "prepend|attach_metadata|synthetic_turn",
  "signature": "sha256:..."  // optional HMAC for auditing
}
Response: 202 Accepted / {"insertion_id": "pid-...", "applied": "best_effort|applied|queued"}

Semantics notes:
- apply_mode:
  * prepend: insert primer as a synthetic user/system turn at head of request queue for next generation call. Affects KV.
  * attach_metadata: store primer as session metadata only; runtime may consult metadata but KV unchanged.
  * synthetic_turn: force immediate generation with primer -> produced tokens appended into KV, optionally cached.
- scope controls visibility: "user" applies only if session belongs to the same user id; "tenant" is visible to all sessions in tenant (careful).
- TTL: best effort; expired primers should not be applied.
- Ordering: primers get insertion_id + timestamp. Edge must fence concurrent primers with a simple vector: latest-primer-wins if priorities equal; high priority can preempt.

Runtime implementation sketch:
- Edge proxy receives primer request and writes a PrimerRecord to session-store (etcd or session-db) under key sessions/{sid}/primers/{insertion_id}. Record = {insertion_id, primer_blob, apply_mode, ttl, requester, signature, created_at, status}.
- Session-manager notices new primer (watch) and attempts to claim it via a lease. If claimed, the manager coordinates with the model runtime:
   * For prepend: manager issues a synthetic generation request with role=\"system/assistant\" depending on apply_mode. It sets a special flag \"primer-ingestion\" so runtime treats tokens as non-billable or marked.
   * For attach_metadata: manager updates session metadata only.
- KV coherence constraint: primer ingestion must not evict or rewrite unrelated KV shards. We append to per-session KV; runtime maintains primer-token-range tag so observability can filter.

Security and auth:
- Primer writes require a scoped token (primer:write). Auditor shall log insertion_id, signer, and request-id.
- Optionally include a signature field (HMAC over payload with tenant key) for high-trust tenants.
- Disallow tenant-scoped primers by default; require explicit enterprise opt-in.

Telemetry / metrics to track:
- primer.requests.total, primer.requests.accepted, primer.requests.rejected
- primer.apply.latency (edge -> session-manager -> runtime)
- primer.effect.delta.early-turn-quality: % improvement in top-level eval metrics for first 3 turns (A/B test).
- primer.kv-growth: avg tokens added by primers per session.
- primer.conflicts.count: number of primers dropped due to race/expiry.

Observability artifacts:
- Primer event envelope logged to tracing as event "primer.inject" with insertion_id and session_id.
- Copiable diagnostics: /admin/sessions/{sid}/primers/{insertion_id} returns record + replay log.

Rollout plan (experimental):
1) Internal experiment: enable for 10% of dev traffic. Use apply_mode=attach_metadata initially. Monitor telemetry and any SLO regressions.
2) Canary: Expand to 1% of prod traffic with synthetic_turn for a small model variant.
3) Full test: A/B against baseline for early-turn perplexity and token cost.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do primers interact with model-level context windows when session already near max_seq? (eviction policy?)
- Billing: mark primer-driven tokens as non-billable for customer during experiment or bill normally? Need finance input (JIRA INF-3502).
- Auditability: retention policy for primer records (default 30d?)
- Client ergonomics: should we support a client-side helper to create condensed primers (summary generator) or rely on server side?

Quick ascii diagram:
Client ---> Edge Proxy (primer API) ---> Session-store (writes primer record)
                                         |
                                         v
                                 Session-manager (claim + coordinate) ---> Runtime (synthetic ingestion / metadata)

Notes on experiments:
- Start with primers that are summaries of the last 3 user turns (max 150 tokens). Test 3 variants: 
  A) system prompt prepend, B) attach_metadata, C) synthetic_turn then discard.
- Measure median latency increase for apply path; target < 30ms added for attach_metadata path, <150ms for synthetic ingestion.

References / related tickets:
- INF-3421: primer API spike
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prs/1234 (initial edge change)
- Slack thread: #session-runtime (thread ts 1695212345.000100)

Short-term action items (this week):
- [ ] implement edge accept + write to session-store (Marco)
- [ ] session-manager watch + simple claimant (Ling)
- [ ] eval harness for early-turn quality (Aisha)
- [ ] privacy review for tenant-scoped primers (sec/compliance)
